sections.content:
Population change in Richmond upon Thames in 2032

The population in Richmond upon Thames is projected to increase from 195,165 people in 2022 to 198,834 people in 2032.

Despite an overall increase in the population, there is projected to be a fall in net internal migration, which will decrease the population by 10,182 people.

This will also be the biggest factor in population change in most areas in England.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in Richmond upon Thames
sections.subtitle: How the population is projected to change, by cause
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant
sections.note: The components of change do not always sum exactly to the total population change in an area. This is primarily due to the effect of constraining the final projections to the National Population Projections for England.

sections.content:
Population change is projected by looking at births and deaths (natural change) and people moving in and out of areas. In Richmond upon Thames, our projections show that between 2022 and 2032:

  • More births than deaths mean that the population is projected to increase by 5,582, with 19,130 births and 13,548 deaths in Richmond upon Thames between 2022 and 2032. This means natural change would increase the population in Richmond upon Thames by 2.9%, compared with an increase of 6.0% in London and an increase of 0.2% in England.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other local authorities in England) is projected to reduce the population by 10,182, with 165,145 people moving to the area and 175,327 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would decrease the population in Richmond upon Thames by 5.2%.
  • Net cross-border migration (between UK nations) is projected to reduce the population by 1,169, with 4,440 people moving to the area and 5,609 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would decrease the population in Richmond upon Thames by 0.6%.
  • Net international migration is projected to increase the population by 9,297, with 29,764 people moving to the area and 20,467 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population in Richmond upon Thames by 4.8%, compared with an increase of 14.7% in London and an increase of 6.5% in England.

sections.content:
Age profile in Richmond upon Thames in 2032

The median age in Richmond upon Thames is projected to rise from 42 years in 2022 to 44 years in 2032.

In England, the median age is projected to be 41 years in 2032.

In 2032, 19% of the population in Richmond upon Thames are projected to be aged 65 years or over, up from 16% in 2022.

sections.title: The 0 to 9 age group are set to see the largest change in Richmond upon Thames between 2022 and 2032
sections.subtitle: Percentages of population by 10 year age bands, 2022 and 2032
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant

sections.content:
Between 2022 and 2032, the share of the working age population (people aged 16 years to State Pension age) in Richmond upon Thames is projected to stay the same, at around 65%.

The old age dependency ratio (the number of people of State Pension age for every 1,000 people of working age) is projected to rise from 243 to 266 over the same time period.

This is below average for England in 2032 (287 per 1,000). Nationally, a high old age dependency ratio means more older people are financially reliant on the working age population to pay for pensions.

How will the number of young people change in Richmond upon Thames?

In 2032, 19% of people are projected to be aged 18 years and under, down from 24% in 2022.

This is below average for England in 2032 (20%).

Looking at the youngest age groups in Richmond upon Thames between 2022 and 2032, we can see the share of:

  • Infants (aged 0 to 4 years) will fall from 6% to 5%
  • Primary school age children (aged 5 to 11 years) will fall from 9% to 7%
  • Secondary school age children and sixth-form age (aged 12 to 18 years) will fall from 9% to 8%
